skill.name: CRUD with Spec-Kit
skill.description: Guides specification-driven CRUD implementation with Spec-Kit and AI coding tools.
skill.summary: Turn clear entity specifications into consistent CRUD implementation plans, routes, clients, validation, and tests.
skill.author: Claude

security_audit.summary: The reviewed skill is prompt-only documentation describing specification-driven CRUD development. No static findings were supplied, and no prompt-injection, data-exfiltration, or business-logic abuse intent was found in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: CRUD work can become inconsistent when requirements, APIs, clients, and tests are designed separately. This skill guides a specification-driven workflow for planning and generating aligned CRUD implementation artifacts.
actual_capabilities: Interprets entity attributes, relationships, constraints, and required CRUD operations from specifications.
Plans REST endpoints with suitable HTTP methods, response formats, and error handling.
Outlines backend request validation and data-access patterns that match stated requirements.
Generates guidance for frontend API clients, data models, service layers, and CRUD interface components.
Maps success criteria to implementation checks, gap analysis, and test cases.
Recommends consistent project structure and reusable scaffolding patterns.
limitations: It is conceptual guidance and does not include executable generators or framework-specific templates.
It requires complete, stable specifications with clear entities, constraints, and success criteria.
It does not replace security review, authorization design, database migration planning, or production testing.
Generated suggestions require review for the target language, framework, and data model.

use_cases.title: Plan a new API resource
use_cases.description: Convert a product specification for one entity into CRUD routes, validations, responses, and acceptance checks.

use_cases.title: Align client and server work
use_cases.description: Define matching API client methods, data models, and interface states from the same CRUD specification.

use_cases.title: Review feature completeness
use_cases.description: Compare an existing CRUD implementation with its specification and identify missing operations, validations, or tests.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: outline CRUD operations
prompt_templates.scenario: Start from a simple entity definition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this entity specification, list the Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations. Include required fields, validation rules, and expected responses: [paste specification]

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: design REST routes
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an API plan before coding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this CRUD specification into a REST API design. For every endpoint, provide the method, path, request fields, success response, error cases, and validation requirements: [paste specification]

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: plan full-stack implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on this specification, produce a full-stack CRUD implementation plan. Cover backend routes, data access, API client methods, UI states, validation, error handling, and tests. State assumptions clearly: [paste specification]

prompt_templates.title: Expert: assess specification compliance
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a completed feature against its requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the implementation summary below with the specification. Produce a traceability matrix for each requirement, mark it as implemented, partial, or missing, and recommend prioritized fixes and tests. Specification: [paste] Implementation: [paste]

output_examples.input: A Product has name, price, stock quantity, and an optional description.
output: CRUD scope: create, list, retrieve by identifier, update, and delete products.
Validation: name is required, price is non-negative, and stock quantity is a non-negative integer.
Testing: cover valid creation, invalid price, missing name, updates, retrieval of absent records, and deletion.

output_examples.input: Review an implementation that has create and list endpoints but no update endpoint.
output: Status: partial compliance because the Update operation is missing.
Recommended work: add an update route with validation and a not-found response.
Required tests: valid update, invalid input, and update for a missing record.

best_practices: Provide entity definitions, constraints, relationships, and success criteria before requesting implementation guidance.
Review generated API contracts with backend and frontend stakeholders before writing code.
Treat generated code and tests as a starting point, then validate security, authorization, and production behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use incomplete specifications as the only source of truth for data validation or business rules.
Do not expose CRUD endpoints without designing authentication, authorization, and input validation.
Do not assume generated scaffolding matches a project architecture without code review and testing.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It guides specification-driven planning and implementation of Create, Read, Update, and Delete features.

faq.question: Does it generate executable code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides conceptual guidance and prompts for AI-assisted code generation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input produces the best results?
faq.answer: Use a clear specification with entities, fields, constraints, relationships, operations, and success criteria.

faq.question: Can it design both backend and frontend work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers API routes, validation, data access, client methods, models, and interface components.

faq.question: Does it handle security requirements?
faq.answer: It mentions validation and error handling, but you must separately design and review authentication, authorization, and security controls.
